approval_record.authority_statement: This object is approved governance knowledge. Legal interpretation, finding lock, residual-risk acceptance, tactic execution and lifecycle authorization remain attributable decisions under the defined human authority boundary.
approval_record.change_control: A semantic or mapping change requires a new version, reciprocal validation and renewed approval.

title: Prompt-only or model-mediated security boundary
canonical_definition: A security-critical restriction depends mainly on instructions, refusals, model behavior or unverified model-mediated filters instead of independently enforceable controls and representative adversarial evidence.
failure_mechanism: Untrusted data or model output influences a security-relevant decision while the principal restriction is probabilistic or controlled by the same model-mediated path. An attacker may therefore manipulate the mechanism expected to provide protection.
potential_consequences: Unauthorized tool use or state change
Unsafe downstream code, markup, query or command execution

conditions: Screen every AI solution for model-mediated security boundaries.

Assess as applicable when the system processes untrusted or attacker-influenced model inputs, retrieved content or generated outputs and a reachable path can affect confidentiality, integrity, availability, safety, authorization or a material decision.
Assess as not applicable only when architecture and test evidence establish that no model-influenced path reaches a security-relevant boundary.

primary_questions.question: Are any security-critical restrictions expressed mainly as prompts, model policies, refusals or model-mediated filters rather than independently enforceable controls?
Can untrusted input, retrieved content or generated output influence tools, data, privileges, interpreters or consequential decisions beyond the authorized boundary?
Do representative adversarial tests establish presence or tested absence across the scoped attack surface, versions, identities, integrations and bypass paths?

atomic_tests.title: Safety-prompt and refusal dependency inspection
atomic_tests.description: Trace every security-relevant restriction to the component that enforces it and identify restrictions enforced only through prompts, refusals or model behavior.

atomic_tests.title: Direct and indirect instruction-injection test
atomic_tests.description: Exercise direct prompts, retrieved content, uploaded files, external content and other attacker-influenced instructions against reachable security boundaries.

atomic_tests.title: Model-output to interpreter, tool and action trace
atomic_tests.description: Trace generated output into downstream parsers, interpreters, queries, tools, APIs and state-changing actions.

atomic_tests.title: Tool argument and authorization bypass test
atomic_tests.description: Test whether model-generated tool selection, destinations or arguments can exceed deterministic allowlists, identity checks, scopes or transaction limits.

atomic_tests.title: Retrieval, upload, browser and memory poisoning test
atomic_tests.description: Test whether untrusted persistent or retrieved content can alter privileged behavior during the same or later sessions.

atomic_tests.title: Fallback and secondary-path bypass test
atomic_tests.description: Exercise retry, cache, fallback, error, degraded-service and secondary execution paths using realistic identities and permissions.

atomic_tests.title: Sensitive-data and tenant-isolation test
atomic_tests.description: Test unauthorized disclosure across users, tenants, tools, memory, logs and provider boundaries.

atomic_tests.title: Detection, containment and recovery verification
atomic_tests.description: Verify security-relevant activity is logged, alertable, containable and recoverable without relying on model cooperation.

antipattern_indicators: A safety prompt or model refusal is presented as the principal security control.
Free-form model output reaches tools, interpreters, queries or external actions without deterministic mediation.
Untrusted retrieved, uploaded, browser or memory content can alter privileged behavior.
No representative adversarial testing covers the application, retrieval, tool and identity context.
A validator or policy component accepts model-defined destinations, permissions or operations outside an allowlist.
Content scanning is presented as complete protection despite reachable secondary or encoded bypass paths.
Only the model endpoint is tested while the surrounding application and downstream effects are excluded.

required_evidence.title: Security-boundary architecture and data-flow record
required_evidence.description: Versioned architecture identifies untrusted inputs, model-mediated paths, protected assets, trust boundaries, identities, privileges, tools and downstream actions.

required_evidence.title: Deterministic enforcement evidence
required_evidence.description: Code and configuration demonstrate external authorization, validation, allowlisting, least privilege and isolation for security-relevant effects.

required_evidence.title: Representative adversarial execution record
required_evidence.description: Executed tests record scope, identities, privileges, integrations, versions, attack corpus, raw results, failures and retest status.

required_evidence.title: Operational detection and containment evidence
required_evidence.description: Operational records demonstrate logging, alerting, containment, recovery and ownership for relevant attack and failure paths.

absence_test_requirements: Define the exact model-influenced, untrusted-input and security-relevant surfaces in scope.
Identify every protected asset, identity, privilege, integration, downstream interpreter and state-changing action in that scope.
Confirm that security decisions and privileged actions are enforced outside model discretion.
Execute representative direct and indirect manipulation tests using realistic identities, privileges, data and downstream integrations.
Include secondary, fallback, cache, retry, degraded-service and error paths.
Record versions, configurations, attack corpus, thresholds, raw results and known limitations.
Independently verify the test scope and successful result.
Use TESTED_ABSENT only for the tested surface, configuration, version and time; never claim universal immunity.

confirmed_present: Verified code, configuration or architecture evidence establishes that a security-critical restriction is principally model-mediated.
A representative executed test demonstrates a material bypass or exploit path crossing a protected boundary.
partially_present: A model-mediated restriction exists, but independently enforced controls materially bound its reachable effect.
A demonstrated manipulation changes behavior without yet establishing a material protected-boundary crossing.
tested_absent: The defined reachable surface is covered by verified architecture evidence and a scoped, successful, representative adversarial test record.
All security-relevant decisions and effects in scope are independently enforced outside model discretion.
unknown: No material exploit is shown, but coverage, realistic privileges, versions, integrations or secondary paths are insufficient.
Implementation is visible but executed adversarial results or their scope are unavailable.
contradictory: Documentation claims deterministic enforcement while code, configuration, permissions or executed results show model-controlled behavior.
Different sources describe incompatible trust boundaries, privileges or reachable effects.
assurance_ceilings: Prompts, policies, design statements and model refusals are DECLARED and cannot establish IMPLEMENTED or TESTED assurance.
Code and configuration may establish IMPLEMENTED assurance but not operational effectiveness.
A test file without attributable execution results cannot establish TESTED assurance.
Operational effectiveness requires attributable operational evidence for the assessed version and environment.

false_positive_guards: A system prompt is not proof of this anti-pattern when it is only a usability layer and every security-relevant effect is independently enforced.
A successful instruction injection is not necessarily material when it cannot cross a protected boundary; record the reachable consequence and asset.
Lack of a red-team report does not alone confirm the anti-pattern; it establishes an assurance gap unless other evidence proves the boundary is model-mediated.
A content-filter failure does not prove the complete boundary is model-mediated when deterministic downstream controls contain the effect.
Editorial differences in control names do not establish contradictory architecture when the enforced mechanism and scope are equivalent.
prohibited_inferences: A provider guardrail proves application security.
Human review proves authorization cannot be manipulated.
A policy statement proves the control is enabled in the assessed environment.
Remediation activity completion changes the anti-pattern state without new evidence and reassessment.

conditions: Exploitation can execute privileged or irreversible actions.
Exploitation can expose sensitive multi-tenant, personal or special-category data.
Exploitation can alter a safety function or consequential decision.
A demonstrated path has uncontrolled external effects or materially defeats required human authority.

hard_gate_effect.CONFIRMED_PRESENT: Block Deployment and Operation when a material security-relevant path is reachable. Require deterministic containment, new evidence and reassessment before progression.
hard_gate_effect.PARTIALLY_PRESENT: Require human Security review and condition progression on bounded exposure, verified containment, monitoring and time-bound remediation.
hard_gate_effect.UNKNOWN: Block Deployment and Operation when the untested surface can reach a high-consequence boundary. Earlier work remains within an isolated environment until evidence closes the uncertainty.
hard_gate_effect.CONTRADICTORY: Block progression until the contradiction is resolved through verified implementation and test evidence.
hard_gate_effect.TESTED_ABSENT: Do not create an independent positive assurance conclusion. The paired D3 capability must still meet its lifecycle target.

normative_source_mappings.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (Artificial Intelligence Act)
normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: Supports the requirement, when applicable, to resist unauthorized exploitation of AI-system vulnerabilities.

normative_source_mappings.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile
normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: Supports red-teaming and continuing verification of information-security measures.

normative_source_mappings.relevant_locator: AI-specific augmentation of SP 800-218 practices and tasks
normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: Supports secure implementation and verification of model and application boundaries.

normative_source_mappings.title: Guidelines for Secure AI System Development
normative_source_mappings.relevant_locator: Secure design, development, deployment, and operation and maintenance
normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: Supports enforceable security across the AI-system lifecycle.

normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: Supports the modeled failure mechanisms for instruction injection, unsafe output, excessive agency and retrieval weaknesses.

normative_source_mappings.title: Multilayer Framework for Good Cybersecurity Practices for AI
normative_source_mappings.mapping_rationale: Supports AI-specific rather than purely generic cybersecurity analysis.

finding_definitions.title: Security-critical restriction relies primarily on prompt or model behavior
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Deployment and Operation remain blocked when the reachable effect is material.

finding_definitions.title: Untrusted content crosses a privileged, sensitive or execution boundary
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Deployment and Operation remain blocked until deterministic containment is verified.

finding_definitions.title: Representative adversarial testing confirms exploitability of the model-mediated boundary
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: The affected transition remains blocked until the exploit path is removed, retested and independently verified.

finding_definitions.title: Tested absence cannot be substantiated for the assessed attack surface
finding_definitions.lifecycle_consequence: Deployment and Operation remain blocked when the untested surface can reach a high-consequence boundary.

runtime_decision_boundary.ai_role: AI may extract evidence, identify candidate signals and propose a traceable assessment interpretation.
runtime_decision_boundary.deterministic_role: Applicability, assurance ceilings, conclusion-state rules, finding triggers, hard gates and tactic eligibility are applied deterministically.
runtime_decision_boundary.human_role: Named human authorities resolve legal interpretation, lock consequential findings, accept residual risk and authorize lifecycle transitions.
prohibited: AI narrative cannot waive a hard gate.
A readiness score cannot authorize progression.
Tactic assignment or completion cannot change a finding state.

domain_title: Architecture, security, robustness, safety and evaluation
